> •  A two-wheeled camera robot you can control with your phone.•   For the longest time I have wanted to create a remote-controlled car of some sort. Once I found out that with Half Club/Half-Life can help fund projects I went to work to brainstorm. My hope is that this can help me create a prototype for a two wheeled bot with which I can make for a local  tech I help host at my small school during the summer and if I can get this to work I would be really excited.   PicoScout1 is not just any robot but I wanted a small robot that can be good to use for tech camp or anyone really but my plan is to make it so that I can control it with a phone and be able to move the robot and see what the camera sees which can make for some fun for really anyone to play with *If it works*. This is my first project with Hack Club but it will not be my first but second PCB I designed yet motors will be a new thing for me. Also Week 1 ends up also being when I have a break off of school so I can devote more time upfront.

## Design

### 2026-10-10 – Monday-Wednesday of Week 1

**9h**

Monday-Wednesday of Week 1

  ![IMG_09369L9QLx](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/4bZAgAzJChvltfdcABNWdCwEvUfJDmZw/776addef0152c7e2eac01ae3856b585749d9537e66284ac26d18484c4599f140.png)

![IMG_09358zrASb](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/4bZAgAzJChvltfdcABNWdCwEvUfJDmZw/44cf0a94fd917de8a846d522c30c3c44cb84cbf6fd1669e25a86a861d3fcc4bc.png)

   I did a lot of research trying to figure out what parts to use for my PicoScout1. I ended up deciding that N20 motors are my best bet for this project and I was going to use the Xiao esp32 S3 for the camera and to control the robot. I used EasyEDA which I have used for 1 other PCB project but there were so many things I still did not know. I spent multiple hours just trying to import components into EasyEDA which they do not have in their list of components like the motors and the xiao esp32 S3.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 at 4.02.18 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/4bZAgAzJChvltfdcABNWdCwEvUfJDmZw/a38bd4bdcd787de758cbf90d6db749aeb21bc8669089bc67c4a9b41aa02514ea.png)
I found this project on https://hackaday.io/project/175378-3d-printable-antweight-battlebot-bulldog/details along with other projects like Micromouse but this one in particular was the one that encouraged me to use the N20 motors for my project.

![IMG_0934HWAyH6](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/4bZAgAzJChvltfdcABNWdCwEvUfJDmZw/f3721b5aeb28f9aa612960ff195e8491db168665913964060386e100f5822e60.png)

 I started on my first design and something happened and it got messed up so it disappeared but I did print the design of what I had at one point which I have.  I thought I could make a two PCB sandwich with the motors and the battery in the center.

   However that is not the design I stuck with but I decided for a 2 wheel approach on the pcb with the idea being that it will go inside a 3d printed case. I had AI help me with how to wire some of these parts and find them for me because I had no prior knowledge of how to make a 3.7 to 6v boost converter which I added and the motor controller for the two wheels.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 at 2.40.10 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/4bZAgAzJChvltfdcABNWdCwEvUfJDmZw/59fdeb52f8e6b66d1a8746435c7aa47544fafc0c18e7110e401991aa88154a8c.png)
